subject: Post-call: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency & throughput benchmarks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@globex.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:05:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency & throughput benchmarks

Thanks again for taking the time today, John - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the A/B benchmark started:

Summary from call:
- Globex is focused on conversational agents for customer support with strict p95 latency targets (< 250ms) for short-turn queries and p99 targets for peak traffic windows.
- Main competitors you’re evaluating are the major hyperscaler managed endpoints and one other inference provider.
- Key metrics you asked us to prioritize: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (throughput), and cost per effective 1K tokens under your workload.

What we ran (attached): redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks.csv contains our initial microbenchmarks using your sample prompts (n=1k warmup, 5k measured). Highlights:
- Redwood (dedicated quantized profile): p95 = 180ms, p99 = 320ms, tokens/sec = 210
- Hyperscaler X (standard endpoint): p95 = 240ms, p99 = 470ms, tokens/sec = 140
- Notes: measurements done on 8k context, batch size 4, cooled JVM overhead minimized. See CSV for raw samples and redwood_latency_plots.png for percentile graphs.

Proposed A/B test (what we recommend for parity with your infra):
1) Test window: 2 hours of sustained load (traffic shape you provided) + 30m warmup.
2) Variants: Redwood Dedicated (quantized) vs Hyperscaler standard endpoint; both pinned to the same model family/config.
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency timeline, tokens/sec, errors, and cost/1K tokens.
4) Configs: batch sizes {1,4,8}, concurrency ramp (0->400 RPS over 20m), same tokenizer/version.
5) Deliverables: CSV of raw samples, aggregated percentile reports, Grafana snapshot, and a short summary slide.

Next steps / actions:
- Please confirm test window (we suggested Wed 2026-07-14 10:00-12:30 PT) and share any updated sample traffic or auth needed for the Hyperscaler endpoint.
- We’ll share a short test plan (attached: globex_test_plan.md) and a link to our results drive.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks.csv, globex_test_plan.md, redwood_latency_plots.png

Thanks - I’ll coordinate the kickoff once we have the confirmed window.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-11T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency & throughput benchmarks

Marissa - thanks for the detailed recap and for the attachments. A few quick clarifications before we lock the window:

1) Batch sizes: Are the numbers in the CSV per-request batch or per-GPU-batch? We need per-request numbers to map to our front-end collector.
2) Warmup: can you confirm what you used for the 1k warmup (unique prompts vs repeats)? We want warmup to mimic traffic (not identical repeated prompts).
3) Access: We can provision access to the Hyperscaler endpoint and a short-lived key for your test runner - I’ll send the link once Priya confirms.

Wed 07/14 10:00 PT works for us provisionally - can you also include cost calc per 1M tokens for both variants in the final report? That’s a hard ask from procurement.

John
Director, Platform Engineering | Globex Corporation
john.smith@globex.com | +1 617-555-3321

Adding a couple of notes on execution and what we’ll capture so there’s no surprises:

- Batch semantics: our runner reports per-request latency (time from request sent to first byte of token stream) and GPU-batch size separately. CSV has both columns - we’ll include a short mapping table.
- Warmup: we’ll do a warmup set with 1k unique prompts sampled from your corpus (not repeated). For reproducibility, we’ll seed the sampling and share the seed.
- Percentile capture: we’ll report p50/p90/p95/p99 and also provide a tail-latency timeline (1m buckets) so you can see when spikes occur.
- Tokenization: we’ll use the same tokenizer binary you provided (tokenizer v2.1). Please confirm the model checkpoint variant to pin for both endpoints.
- Cost calc: Marissa, we’ll include cost/1M tokens for expected qps shapes and show both steady-state and burst scenarios.

Runner snippets we’ll use (k6-style):
- warmup: ./runner --seed=34782 --prompts=1000 --batch=4 --dur=10m
- main: ./runner --prompts=5000 --concurrency=400 --dur=2h --collect-percentiles

I’ll take the lead on running the Redwood side and Aditya will coordinate the Hyperscaler traffic if we need an extra runner.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

All good - we’ve provisioned the Hyperscaler test key and Priya shared the endpoint details in the Doc we sent (see drive link). Confirmed for Wed 07/14 10:00 PT.

A few final asks from procurement/security:
- Please share SOC2 evidence bundle link (we have a checklist item) - if you can point to the SOC2 report or our vendor portal, that’d speed review.
- Can you include a short note in the kickoff slide about fallback behavior (if Redwood falls back to a cheaper instance during the run) - our SREs want to understand deterministic behavior during the A/B test.

We’ll be on the call at 10:00 PT; Priya and I will monitor the Grafana dashboard. Thanks for coordinating.

John
